head: feat/tax
title: Apply sales tax at checkout with cent-precision rounding

summary.headline: Adds applyTax (cent-rounded) and wires it into the pricing total.
summary.why: Two commits: a new applyTax helper with floating-point-safe cent rounding, and a pricing change that now adds tax to the subtotal. The helper is also exported for tests; money.ts adds shared cent conversion helpers and tests/calc.test.ts locks the rounding behaviour.

perFile.note: New applyTax helper: raw = amount * rate then Math.round(raw*100)/100; also logs the raw amount.
Total now includes tax via applyTax(subtotal, TAX_RATE).
New shared cents conversion helpers to avoid float drift elsewhere.
New currency formatting helper (non-ASCII path render check).
Unit tests for applyTax rounding, including a repeating-rate case.

risks.title: Floating-point rounding of amount * rate may drift on edge inputs
risks.rationale: Math.round(raw*100)/100 is not exact decimal arithmetic: rates like 1/3 or amounts with many decimals can round unexpectedly. Tests cover 19.99 * 1/3, but amounts near .005 boundaries are untested and binary floats can produce 14.995 -> 15.00 vs 14.99.

risks.title: console.log prints the raw monetary amount
risks.rationale: Raw amounts in server-side logs can be considered sensitive; in enterprise/PCI contexts log content may be retained. Should use the formatted helper or structured logging without the raw value.

risks.title: Pricing total now includes tax — callers may double-charge
risks.rationale: pricing.ts now adds tax to subtotal. Any other code path that already applied tax would now double-charge. Only this file changed, so reviewers should check remaining callers.

happyPath.scenario: applyTax on a normal amount and rate
checkout shows a tax-inclusive total to the customer
happyPath.input: complete {checkout flow} for a tax-inclusive item
happyPath.expected: displayed total includes tax; no double charge

edgeCases.scenario: amount * rate produces a value exactly at a .005 boundary
edgeCases.whyConcern: binary floats: values like 14.995 can round up or down depending on representation; 1/3 rates never terminate
edgeCases.assertion: result matches cent-rounding policy exactly (no silent 0.01 drift); assert explicit expected values

edgeCases.scenario: zero, negative, and very large amounts
edgeCases.whyConcern: float math on extremes can produce NaN/Infinity or unexpected sign handling
edgeCases.assertion: no crash, no NaN, sign preserved or rejected per policy

edgeCases.scenario: log output containing the raw amount is inspected
edgeCases.whyConcern: server logs may retain raw monetary amounts, a PII/PCI concern in enterprise
edgeCases.assertion: logs must not expose raw amount/PII; prefer formatted value or remove log

edgeCases.scenario: this change is reverted after some orders were priced with tax
edgeCases.whyConcern: orders priced during the change window must remain consistent after rollback
edgeCases.assertion: no double-charge state persists; pricing consistent across deploy windows
